quote.text: You know yourself what you are worth in your own eyes; and at what price you will sell yourself. For men sell themselves at various prices. This is why, when Florus was deliberating whether he should appear at Nero's shows, taking part in the performance himself, Agrippinus replied, 'Appear by all means.' And when Florus inquired, 'But why do not you appear?' he answered, 'Because I do not even consider the question.' For the man who has once stooped to consider such questions, and to reckon up the value of external things, is not far from forgetting what manner of man he is.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood: Recognize that the value you see in yourself sets the standard for your children; do not allow the opinions of others to diminish your inner worth.
  • In raising your offspring, teach them to honor their own integrity and to never compromise who they are for the fleeting favor of external validation.
  • Leadership: A true leader remains steadfast in personal virtue, refusing to negotiate principles for the sake of popularity or temporary gains.
  • Lead by example—cultivate an inner strength that inspires others to value their true worth and to act with courage and authenticity in challenging situations.
  • Product Management: In crafting products, let your design reflect the inherent value and authenticity of your vision, without succumbing to trends that compromise quality.
  • Focus on building a product that is true to your integrity; by doing so, you demonstrate that lasting worth is always measured by principle and purpose, not by superficial metrics.
